content.title: About
content.content: Celery is a perennial herbaceous plant of the Apiaceae family cultivated for its crunchy stalks, leaves, and seeds. Raw celery has a crisp texture, mildly bitter, refreshing flavor and very low calorie content. It is used in fresh salads, juices, soups, and as a garnish.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Celery belongs to the same family as carrots, parsley, and dill.
Celery was known in ancient Egypt, where it was used for medicinal purposes.
Celery contains natural phytochemicals called phthalides that may help lower blood pressure.
Celery stalks can grow up to 30 cm long, while the leaf blades can reach 60 cm in width.
Celery is often featured in detox diets because of its diuretic properties.

items.title: Low calorie density
items.content: Raw celery provides about 16 kcal per 100 g, making it an excellent choice for weight management.

items.title: Rich in fiber
items.content: Dietary fiber supports digestion, promotes satiety, and helps maintain a healthy gut microbiome.

items.title: Source of vitamin K
items.content: Vitamin K is essential for blood clotting and bone health.

items.title: Contains vitamins A and C
items.content: These antioxidants support immune function, vision, and protect cells from oxidative stress.

items.title: Phytochemical compounds
items.content: Phthalides and flavonoids may contribute to lower blood pressure and improved cardiovascular function.

items.title: Allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to celery, ranging from skin rashes to swelling.

items.title: Drug interactions
items.content: Celery can enhance the effects of anticoagulants (e.g., warfarin) due to its high vitamin K content.

items.title: Pesticide residues
items.content: As with many vegetables, celery may carry pesticide residues; thorough washing before consumption is recommended.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Raw celery can be eaten as a snack, cut into sticks for dips, added to salads, smoothies, and juices. It also serves as an aromatic base for soups and stews.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store celery in the refrigerator’s vegetable drawer, wrapped in a damp towel or in a perforated plastic bag. When stored properly it stays fresh for up to 2 weeks. Remove any yellowing leaves.

content.title: About
content.content: Shrimp are low‑calorie, high‑protein seafood. Combined with carrots, broccoli and dark‑green leafy vegetables (spinach, kale) the dish provides a wide range of vitamins, minerals and fiber. It is prepared without potatoes or sauce, making it light and nutritious.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Shrimp contain astaxanthin, a powerful antioxidant that gives them their pink hue.
Broccoli is one of the most nutrient‑dense vegetables, rich in vitamin C, K and folate.
Carrots are high in beta‑carotene, which the body converts to vitamin A.
Dark‑green leafy greens such as spinach and kale supply iron, calcium and vitamin K.
Shrimp cook very quickly – usually 2‑3 minutes on a hot pan.

items.title: High‑quality protein
items.content: Shrimp provide complete protein needed for muscle growth and tissue repair.

items.title: Low in saturated fat
items.content: The dish contains very little saturated fat, suitable for low‑fat dietary plans.

items.title: Rich in B‑vitamins
items.content: Shrimp are a good source of vitamin B12, essential for nerve function and blood formation.

items.title: Antioxidant protection
items.content: Broccoli and leafy greens are packed with vitamins C and E and flavonoids that combat free radicals.

items.title: Supports eye health
items.content: Beta‑carotene from carrots and lutein from leafy greens help maintain healthy vision.

items.title: Shellfish allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to shrimp, ranging from skin rash to anaphylaxis.

items.title: Cholesterol content
items.content: Shrimp contain cholesterol, so people with high cholesterol should consume them in moderation.

items.title: Pesticide residues
items.content: Non‑organic vegetables may carry pesticide residues; thorough washing is recommended.

items.title: Fiber digestion
items.content: Large amounts of raw leafy greens can cause gas and bloating in sensitive individuals.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Sauté shrimp over high heat for 2‑3 minutes until pink. Add sliced carrots and broccoli and cook another 4‑5 minutes, then stir in leafy greens and toss briefly until wilted. Season with salt, pepper and a squeeze of lemon if desired.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep fresh shrimp refrigerated and use within 2 days; cooked dish can be stored in an airtight container for up to 3 days. Store vegetables in the crisper drawer after rinsing.
